producer_report.summary: Root cause: a file kept by hand as a mirror of a governing source (shard timings, the decision log, the CI cache key against BUILD_PATHS, the ontology) was tested for its structure only, not its content against the source. Drift reached the final verdict in five jobs. Fix at the origin: `crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs` holds `REGISTRY`, where each hand-kept file is declared with its source and a comparison rule that reads both sides. Four rules, each with a message naming the file and the fix: (a) every `--test` and `--lib` unit on disk has a line in xtask/shard-timings.txt, and the reverse; (b) docs/decisions.md starts with its base bytes; (c) the CI athena-bin hashFiles globs and BUILD_PATHS, parsed from the work tree's status.rs, cover each other both ways; (d) every BRIEF.md or term-source line that names an ontology term as a definition or role is covered by a sense or excuse. The ontology walk moved out of the athena-cli ontology test into mirrors.rs so there is one copy. The registry runs in two places. The producer loop (run/producer.rs) runs the entries a change touches after every report and before verification, and sends a drift back through the shared send-back. The new athena-cli test target `mirrors` runs every entry over the real files plus a drifted fixture per entry, so a new entry with an existing rule needs no other edit. BUILD_PATHS had real drift, so it now has nine roots, matching the CI key; a landing that changes athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml or docs/system-facts.md now triggers the drain rebuild. Added: a producer-brief note, CHANGELOG bullet, appended D158, and the timings line for the new test target. checks.rs is unchanged by design (see unchanged_planned_files).

open_issues: The producer-loop filter is per entry, not per finding: a producer who touches a file an entry watches is charged with that entry's drift already in the base. Stated in D158 and tested (mirrors_drift_already_in_the_base_is_charged_to_a_producer_that_touches_a_watched_file). The unfiltered repo test would fail the job at verification anyway.

Drift shares the single send-back with unmet criteria. A drift still present after the send-back does not stop the job in the loop; the configured `cargo test` fails it at verification through athena-cli --test mirrors.
Rule (b) compares with the base commit's text, so it bites on uncommitted edits only. The pinned hash in crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs still guards committed history.
Registering a new hand-kept mirror is prose-only: nothing finds a hand-kept file with no entry.
Rules (a) derive `--test` and `--lib` units only; `--doc` and `--bin` units stay with xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs.
The `athena-cli --test mirrors 6.00` timing is an estimate, as the file header says for every line.

Files outside the reading's seven deliverables were changed (ontology.rs, run/producer.rs, run/send_back.rs, run/mod.rs, run/tests.rs, tests/drain.rs, main.rs, drain.rs, README.md, briefs.rs, xtask/shard-timings.txt), each for a reason named in `files`. If a narrower change is wanted, the prose-only ones (README.md, main.rs, drain.rs, briefs.rs) can be dropped first.
No file was edited that the brief names as governance (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, tool or lint configuration); ci.yml is read only.
mistakes: My first `every_rule_reports_a_drift_with_the_file_and_the_fix` test expected the wrong fix text for a root removed from BUILD_PATHS (the fix is to add the path to BUILD_PATHS); I corrected the test. The first loop tests also reused one repository for two jobs and failed on 'no change'; fixed with a fresh repository per job.

I started the full `cargo test --locked` in the background with the default limit, and it was killed. I did not restart it. I ran every package separately instead and report the full-suite command as not run.
learnings: The producer shell allows only cargo, git status/diff/log/show, ls, rm, mv and chmod; `cat`, `tail`, `sleep` and reading files outside the working directory are blocked, and the background-task output file cannot be read.
A background `cargo test --locked` gets the default 10-minute limit and is killed if a rebuild contends for the build-directory lock; pass a longer timeout, or run packages separately.
The producer's snapshot is a one-commit git repository, so `snapshot.git().show_file(base, path)` can read the base text of any file while the producer works.
Cargo discovers tests from crates/*/tests/*.rs and tests/*/main.rs; tests/common/mod.rs is not a target. xtask has no src/lib.rs, so it has no --lib unit.
A fake-agent job lands its README edit in the test repository, so a second job in the same test needs a fresh repository or it fails with 'the producer made no change'.
docs/ontology.toml exists in the base with seven terms and no excuses, and its serde (test) and toml_edit (core) readings agree on it.
status::BUILD_PATHS had five roots while the CI athena-bin key hashed nine globs; xtask's policy test already pins the key to the true input set, so the constant was the stale side.
toml_edit reads both `senses = [{...}]` inline arrays and `[[term.senses]]` array-of-tables; the registry's parse_ontology handles both.
desires: A way to read the output file of a background command, or to wait on it, since foreground sleep and reading outside the working directory are blocked.
A longer default time limit for a background `cargo test --locked`, or a note in the brief that the default 10 minutes is shorter than the suite when a rebuild is needed first.
